4. It is at this juncture that the Pre-emptee-Petitioner puts this Court on notice of the history of the two rounds of proceedings and cases stemming from Miscellaneous Case No. 45 of 1987 and culminating in the impugned judgment and order dated 31.3.1997 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 70 of 1994. The matter at issue now, however, according to the Pre-emptee-Petitioner is given that the provisions of Section 96 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act') mandates that a pre-emptor must make parties of co-sharer tenants of holdings and tenancies contiguous to the land transferred, the Pre-emptor's case has from the very beginning been marked by a defect of non-joinder or non-addition of such parties, and the lower appellate court having at the very last stage failed to appropriately determine that matter on the basis of facts and evidence before it, the judgment and order in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 70 of 1994 is now liable to be set aside. 

 6. The Lower Court Records (LCR) have been particularly illuminating in charting the trajectory of the two rounds of proceedings and cases stemming from Miscellaneous Case No. 45 of 1987 with regard to the matter at hand. A perusal of the impugned judgment in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 70 of 1994 reveals how the issue of the joinder or addition of necessary parties was dealt with both by the trial court and the parties at the initial round. Reading the impugned judgment in conjunction with the relevant documents in the LCR it is evident that on 28.8.1988 interrogatories pertaining to non-joinder of necessary parties were addressed to the Pre-emptee to which a response was made on 17.12.1988. The application pertaining to the reply being allowed on 13.2.1989, the Pre-emptor, acting under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, applied on 7.3.1989 for the addition of parties in keeping with the reply so submitted by the Pre-emptee and this was allowed. This provided the essential basis upon which Miscellaneous Case No. 45 of 1987 was initially disposed of on 26.6.1989 resulting in a dismissal of the pre-emption application with a finding that one Fanaullah, ostensibly a co-sharer by purchase from the Pre-emptor's husband, had not been made a party to the case. The LCR reveals that in so disposing of that case the trial court proceeded upon statements given both by the said Fanaullah as D.W.2 and an ostensible admission to that effect by the Pre-emptor P.W.1. A clear reading of that statement of the Pre-emptor given on cross-examination and with objection shows, however, that it falls short of a categorical endorsement of the claimed status of the said Fanaullah as a co-sharer by purchase. The trial court, nevertheless, considered that statement of the Pre-emptor to be of overriding value. Be that as it may, the said decision of the trial court, thereafter, came to be considered in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 35 of 1989 filed by the Pre-emptor. 

 "Order 1, rule 10 provides for addition of party at any stage of the proceedings, either upon or without the application of either party. Where there is non-joinder of a necessary party the Court is empowered to add the necessary party under rule 10 at any stage of the proceeding either upon or without the application of either party. The objection as to non-joinder of necessary parties must be taken at the earliest opportunity by the defendant. Such objection provides an opportunity to the plaintiff to remove the defect by adding parties who were omitted. In taking objection on the ground of non-joinder of necessary parties the defendant is required to furnish the names and particulars of the parties who were omitted from the suit. On the refusal of the plaintiff to implead the parties mentioned in the written statement the question becomes an issue for adjudication by the Court and on adjudication the question becomes decided. In such an event the consequences must follow, that is, the suit becomes liable to be dismissed on the ground of non-joinder of necessary party. In the case of a pre-emption proceeding the law regarding procedure can-not be treated as different. If the pre-emptee or for that matter any of the parties disclose existence of a necessary party and furnishes the necessary particulars, but the pre-emptor still insists not to implead him as a party, consequence on adjudication is the same."
